matches.note: Crush won via chain-link submission-style pin after an unseen attacker (later named Psychio Damento) cut Malice's throat open on the top rope mid-match. Afterward, Adam Lash presented Crush a ceremonial title belt, which Crush refused.

matches.note: King 3933597$ Perfect won the FWA World Heavyweight Championship, two falls to one, the deciding fall by submission.

notes: The second surviving document ('Matches from FWA,' FY0QqqIK3EMJ) recaps the identical two matches verbatim and is registered as the same show's second posting, not a separate card.

name: Chi-Town Rumble

date.source: The post's own live-feed posting date, naming the event as that night's card.

notes: The live-feed lineup announcement only; no results transcript of the card itself survives in the held record (an honest gap). Billed matches: World Title (The Godfather (c) vs. "Jackhammer" JP Steele), North American Title (Merlin vs. Bret Smith), World Tag Team Title (The Goodfellas (c) vs. The Angry Bisons), Cruiserweight Title (The Great Tsunami (c) vs. The Crippler), a Chicago Street Fight (Ares vs. Knightmare), and a 30-man over-the-top Chi-Town Rumble battle royal.

name: FWA Hardcore Times, Issue 1
notes: The fed's own first newsletter: a Steve Gunn champion profile, a Malice interview, a top-ten power ranking and a 'Clotheslines' quotes column citing several other in-fiction personalities (Bobby Heenan, Party Animal) and namechecking two cross-fed wrestlers (Aaron Bell, Kane the Eliminator) whose own tenures are outside the held record's FWA holdings.

name: 1st Annual AOL E-Wrestling Awards
notes: FWA's own broadcast of the wider AOL e-wrestling community's first annual awards show (54 ballots cast), hosted by FWA's own two broadcasters. Winners named (all outside FWA's own roster, community-wide honors): Best E-Wrestler (Adam Lash, USW), Best Tag Team (Manslaughter, USW), and a three-way tie for Best Face (Dan "Flash" Kauffman, Chris Quigley, Zahadum) -- the capture ends mid-broadcast, before further categories. This directly corroborates a workshop file's own already-flagged 'AOL Awards' lead.

name: MWCW Sizzlin' Sunday Night, Part 1
notes: A card from Mid-West Championship Wrestling (MWCW), a second fed the FWA operator ran under the same posting handle, opening with a real-world dedication to the 1997 Grand Forks flood. FWA's own Lancer and The Hunter invade MWCW mid-show to attack Lobo and Ozzy Gruesome, confirming a shared fictional universe (or a shared operator) between the two feds -- the FWA-relevant content this document is served for. The Hunter separately wrestles and beats MWCW's own Scott "Rage" McLane by submission ("The Bullseye"); McLane is MWCW's own wrestler and is not minted to FWA's own roster, so this match is not structured into matches[].

name: MWCW Wednesday Night Warfare, Part Two
notes: A second MWCW card from the same operator, continuing the crossover thread the first card opened; no FWA-billed wrestler appears by name in the surviving portion of this second card. Served as further evidence of the same operator's shared universe, per the serve-on-contextual-value rule.
